West Virginia iGaming Revenue Hits $39.5M in September

Published October 15, 2026 · 3 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

West Virginia's regulated online casinos generated roughly $39.5 million in revenue during September 2026, up 15.5% from the same month a year earlier, according to the state Lottery's weekly revenue filings as reported by Gambling.com on October 14, 2026.

The numbers

The 15.5% year-over-year increase continues a growth pattern that's held up across most of West Virginia's regulated online casino market in 2026, a market that has expanded steadily since iGaming first launched in the state in 2020. West Virginia remains one of the smaller regulated iGaming states by total dollar volume compared to larger markets like New Jersey or Pennsylvania, but its consistent year-over-year growth rate has made it a market operators keep adding capacity to rather than treating as an afterthought.

Why it matters to players

Steady double-digit growth in a smaller iGaming state is one of the more reliable signals that a regulated market is maturing rather than plateauing — more players discovering legal online casino options, existing players spending more consistently, or both. It also comes just days after Games Global entered West Virginia as its fifth U.S. iGaming market, a sign that platform providers still see room to grow in a state many bettors don't think of as a major gambling market.
